reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises for the CrFeCoNiX system. E2 discusses Ti-Al intermetallics, not HEAs; E3 describes Mn-Cr-Fe-Co-Ni oxidation but does not compare Al, Mn, or Si variants; E4 reports improved oxidation resistance in AlCoCrFeNi via microstructural refinement, not selective Al oxidation in single-phase CrFeCoNiX. The specific claims about α-Al2O3 formation, lattice mismatch, and comparative behavior of Mn/Si in this HEA system lack prior evidence.
premises: Al addition to CrFeCoNi forms a continuous, slow-growing, dense α-Al2O3 scale
Mn or Si addition leads to less ordered, rapidly growing, stress-prone oxides
α-Al2O3 has low lattice mismatch and low oxygen diffusivity, suppressing further oxidation and stress
Selective oxidation of the X element governs oxide stability above 900 °C
Baseline CrFeCoNi without X lacks a protective oxide scale
